inlineContent.text: Les tutoriels de Developpement Swift initient au développement d'apps avec Swift et Xcode à tous ceux qui apprennent à construire des apps pour les plateformes Apple.

Découvrez comment les tutoriels de Développement Swift peuvent vous accompagner tout au long du cycle complet de développement d'une application. Passez de la conception et de la création d'applications simples à l'enrichissement de vos applications avec des fonctionnalités intelligentes et bien plus encore.
Utilisez les tutoriles de Développement Swift pour vous aider à construire des apps incroyables.
Ask questions, listen to your users, and define a list of features.
Create an interactive prototype that looks and feels like a fully developed iOS app that’s ready for testing.
Improve the clarity and usability of your app design by observing how people interact with your prototype.
Revisit and strengthen your app design using insights from testing and validation.
Plan, prototype, and design your app.
Get to know Xcode and SwiftUI by creating a prototype of a messaging app. Learn about syntax for Swift and how to use the source editor and preview.
Learn how to build a custom view to create a multiday weather forecast. In your view, you’ll use properties to customize the display for each day.

Build two onboarding screens for an iOS app to learn useful tools for putting views where you want them onscreen and inspecting their size. Define colors in the asset catalog and use them to create gradient backgrounds.
Explore adding buttons to your apps. Learn about Swift closures and their relationship to buttons. Use state properties to update the user interface automatically.
Create a dynamic interface that stores a set of items in an array and displays them using lists. Use text fields and bindings to let people enter text.
Get familiar with some of the tools and technologies you’ll use to create apps.
Define your first data model by making your own custom types, and prove they work correctly with unit tests. Then use your custom types to keep track of scores in a game.
Build a list of your friends’ birthdays, using SwiftData to save and retrieve that data across launches.

Create an app to track friends and their favorite movies using SwiftData to manage the model objects. Use a query to display the items in a list, and make a detail view to edit them. Then learn how to create and display relationships between friends and movies, and explore how to create advanced queries.
Power an alphabet game using Observation. Share a complex data model with many independent views.
Model real-world concepts and relationships by creating and testing your own custom types.
Build a screen to capture text and photo data. Use SwiftData to save entries and build a custom view to display them.
Use your knowledge of Swift and data modeling to make the app more engaging with user experience features.
Add localization and accessibility features to your app. Then debug the app so it’s ready to test.
Build and debug a fully functioning habit-tracking app. Apply coding fundamentals and accessibility principles.
Explore machine learning with the Natural Language framework and sentiment analysis.
Use the Vision and Translation frameworks to identify text in an image and translate it into another language.
Train your own machine learning model with Create ML.
Use Core ML to integrate machine learning models into your app.
Create an app that lets users generate and modify images using the Image Playground framework.
Create a quiz app using streaming responses and guided generation.
Enhance your apps with machine learning and AI.
Create your first visionOS app with a window using SwiftUI.
Create multiple windows in visionOS using SwiftUI. Use ornaments to provide access to frequently used controls without crowding or obscuring window contents.
View 3D content from any angle in the Shared Space using Reality Composer Pro and SwiftUI.
Design app experiences for spatial computing.
Collect the necessary information to get your project ready for testing and publishing.
Test your beta app using TestFlight to receive feedback.
Get your app ready for review and publishing.
Use TestFlight to test your beta app, get feedback, and make improvements. Learn how to prepare your app for publishing when it’s ready.
Find other helpful resources as you develop apps.
Xcode includes tools that show you how your app will look and work, right on your Mac, so you don’t need additional devices for testing.
Browse the latest documentation.
Ask questions on the developer forums.

abstract.text: Develop in Swift Tutorials introduce app development with Swift and Xcode to anyone learning to build apps for Apple platforms.
Start your journey into spatial computing development by building a window scene in visionOS using SwiftUI.

Continue refining the models in Score Keeper by creating a model that keeps track of the game state and resets players’ scores when the game starts. Write unit tests with Swift Testing as you build your app to ensure it works as intended.
Learn how to support system features like Dark Mode and localization.

Create an app that collects opinions on hiking, analyzes the responses, and displays the results visually. Use the Natural Language framework to score text based on its sentiment. Then use Swift Charts to summarize your data visually.

You prepared your beta app for testing with TestFlight, created and uploaded an archive, incorporated tester feedback to build a new version, and learned how to submit your app for review and publish it on the App Store.
You adapted the app to various system settings to support people’s needs and preferences. You also investigated and fixed a bug. As a developer, you’ll rely on debugging skills to improve your apps.
Refine your app idea by talking to people, looking for patterns in the challenges they share, and identifying opportunities to help. This process works for any kind of app.
Create an interactive prototype that’s ready for testing and looks and feels like a fully developed iOS app.
Buttons, state, and closures are key components of SwiftUI. They enable your app to respond to user actions, which lets you create powerful and expressive interfaces.
Start building an app that lets people record moments of gratitude. In this tutorial, you’ll create an entry view with a photo picker. You’ll also model your data and save information for each entry.

In this tutorial, you’ll build a fully functioning iPad game for kids learning to spell, called Alphabetizer. Working with prewritten SwiftUI views, you’ll build a “brain” for the app: a data model that understands the game rules and connects to the user interface. You’ll use observable models to connect the data models and the SwiftUI views.
Use volumes to add a 3D model to your room.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Create 3D models in the Shared Space

abstract.text: Start your app development journey by downloading Xcode and exploring its key sections.
People enjoy engaging with an app that recognizes their achievements. Add badges to the app that can be unlocked by new entries and associate badges with the entry that unlocked them.
Use
, and bindings to create dynamic content.
Extend the Friends’ Favorite Movies project from
to let people create, edit, and delete friends and movies.
You’ve learned to create and delete both friends and movies, display and edit them, and create flexible custom views for them.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Wrap-up: Create, update, and delete data

abstract.text: Use Core ML to import a machine learning model into your app. Add the model you trained in
to a new app that takes details about hikes and displays their likely challenge level.

You built an app that uses machine learning to predict the challenge level of a given trail, and you used Core ML to integrate a custom machine learning model. The app collects input from people using it, and the model makes predictions based on the new data.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Wrap-up: Custom models with Core ML

abstract.text: Reflect on how you made your own type to model the core logic in your app and used unit tests to ensure your app works as expected.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Wrap-up: Custom types and Swift Testing

abstract.text: Create a SwiftUI app by building custom views to make a multiday weather forecast. In your custom view, you’ll use

inlineContent.text: properties

abstract.text: to customize the display for each day.

Practice putting views where you want them and inspecting their size by building two onboarding screens for an iOS app. As you code, play with your own layout, colors, graphics, and text to make this project meaningful to you.
Find out how the coding intelligence features in Xcode can help you write code, fix errors, generate documentation and navigate codebases.
You talked to people to explore your app’s purpose, then shaped its structure by focusing on its essential features.
Reflect on the concepts you’ve learned and get ideas for ways to practice using text and modifiers.
Design an app that not only looks and feels right but also meets people’s needs and expectations.
Create an app that recognizes text in photos of trail signs. Use the Vision and Translation frameworks to extract text from an image and translate it into another language.
Use the Foundation Models framework to access Apple’s on-device large language model and generate structured content for a quiz app.
Prepare your project so others can test your beta app.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Get your beta app ready for testing

abstract.text: Get to know Xcode, Swift, and SwiftUI.
You built a macOS app that generates images of food using programmatically created prompts. You included interactive features to refine the images by adding and removing ingredients.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Wrap-up: Image generation with Image Playground

abstract.text: You built an app that leverages Apple’s on-device large language model using the Foundation Models framework. Your app creates quizzes with questions and answers. You also built a state-aware UI that shows whether the selected answer is correct.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Wrap-up: Intelligent features with Foundation Models

abstract.text: Learn to resolve bugs with unit tests and the Xcode debugger.
Refine your design systematically, anchoring every change to design principles and findings from your discovery, prototyping, testing, and validation experiences.
You refined your app’s appearance and behavior based on what you learned from user testing.
The SwiftUI layout system has a few simple rules, but its ultimate behavior can be complex. By combining stacks, spacers, and padding, you can build expressive interfaces.
Text entry and displaying a list of items are features of many apps. When you combine these skills with managing a dynamic data set, you can explore even more kinds of apps.

Xcode offers the tools you need to develop, test, and distribute apps for Apple platforms. Discover Xcode features, explore hands-on tutorials, and start transforming your ideas to apps — at your own pace.
Create an app to keep track of scores while playing games and see how custom types can make your data modeling easier.
Reflect on how you made your first data type to model players and their scores.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Wrap-up: Model data with custom types

abstract.text: You trained a new machine learning model. You used metrics to assess your model’s performance, and you used Create ML to compare your model’s results to your training data to evaluate your model’s accuracy.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Wrap-up: Model training with Create ML

abstract.text: Reflect on how you created a
data model, powered a user interface using that model, and then used SwiftData to save that data across launches.

Machine learning can process and make sense of text in different ways, like embedding or classifying words. You used it to analyze the sentiment behind a body of text, then displayed the data in a visual summary.

In this tutorial, you’ll create an app that lists friends and movies, letting people navigate to a detail screen for each one. In the two following tutorials, you’ll extend the app to let people add and edit existing data, create relationships between friends and movies, and build a search interface.
You’ve learned to create and manage sample data that you can use as you build the user interface of a SwiftData app. You also used tabs and navigation split views to navigate complex information.
You created a relationship between the friend and movie models. Related models let people create richer app data. You also created a dynamic query to power a search interface.
Alphabetizer is your first iPad app and your first game. You defined data models separate from SwiftUI views using
. Then you connected and shared those data models across multiple independent SwiftUI views.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Wrap-up: Observation and shareable data models

abstract.text: Identify your app’s essential features to define its structure. Then decide how to organize them and plan how people will navigate through your app.
Design apps specifically for visionOS by creating multiple windows and using ornaments to keep the user interface clean and easy to use.
In this tutorial, you’ll create an app that uses controls in an ornament to design labels that can be placed around the room. Each time you create a label, you’ll create a window in 3D space.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Present common controls in an ornament

abstract.text: You built an interactive prototype, moving from abstract ideas to something concrete that people can test. Along the way, you answered key questions about your app design: Does the flow make sense? Do people know where they are and what they can do next?
Machine learning can process and analyze images and video using computer vision. You used it to recognize and translate text found in images.

Explore data modeling for the first time by building an app that displays your friends and their birthdays. Start by creating a model to represent the data, then integrate with the SwiftData framework so you can save data between launches of the app.
You’ve built your app and tested it thoroughly. To make it publicly available on the App Store, submit it for review. Follow Apple’s guidelines to help ensure a smooth release.
Review the features of Swift that are essential to completing these tutorials.
Ask people to complete a task with your prototype. Plan your testing session, observe how they interact, and ask questions to check your assumptions.
Create and upload an archive of your project. Then, send your beta app to testers and refine it by incorporating feedback.

You identified a key task to test, planned your sessions, and observed how people used your prototype to spot friction. Then you analyzed the results to find opportunities to improve how your app functions.

Discover how easy it is to train a machine learning model with Create ML. Using provided data, train a model to predict how challenging a trail is based on characteristics like distance and elevation.
Explore how

properties and buttons work to update the UI of your app by creating an app to roll virtual dice. Add the functionality to increase or decrease the number of dice on the screen to play different kinds of games.
Continue the Grateful Moments demo app by displaying entries in a list and building a custom hexagon layout to show each entry’s details.
You added complementary features that encourage engagement with the app.
Build an app that lets people generate and customize images. Use the Image Playground framework to create an initial image and accept user input to modify it.
Turn feedback from testing with people into insights. Use those insights to refine your design.
You combined what you learned in
and
along with new ideas to create an app that supports people in building a habit.
Reflect on how you used a structure to create a custom view and used properties to pass arguments to the view’s initializer to customize each instance.

When you add 3D objects using volumes, you let people view content from all angles. Volumes also create an experience that transitions fluidly from a 2D window into a more immersive scene with 3D content.

Develop in Swift Tutorials introduce app development with Swift and Xcode to anyone learning to build apps for Apple platforms. Build great-looking apps with SwiftUI, use Apple Intelligence to unlock new experiences, dive into machine learning and spatial computing, and more.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Welcome to Develop in Swift Tutorials

abstract.text: SwiftUI helps you build great-looking apps across all Apple platforms with the power of Swift — and surprisingly little code. Get to know SwiftUI as you build prototypes, app screens, and fully functioning apps.
Turn your ideas into an intuitive iOS app design. Discover what people need, design features that meet those needs, and build interactive prototypes ready for testing.

Build a complete iOS app. Create a data model and connect it to SwiftUI views, implement navigation, and add an achievements feature integrated throughout your app. Enable inclusive features, learn to debug your code, and make your app more engaging.
When your beta app is ready, prepare and upload it for testing. You can also submit your app for review and publishing.
Learn how to represent real-world concepts as models in code. You’ll create data models with your own Swift types, using a variety of techniques to power your apps.

Explore the basics of machine learning and learn how to add intelligent features to your apps with Apple tools and frameworks. Create and train your own models using Create ML and Core ML. Use the on-device models to generate content in your app with the Foundation Models and Image Playground frameworks.

doc://com.apple.DevelopInSwift/tutorials.title: Welcome to machine learning and AI

abstract.text: Dive into the future of computing with visionOS. Whether you’re a student eager to explore the next frontier or a developer looking to revolutionize your applications, Develop in Swift Tutorials will get you up and running with Apple’s platform for spatial computing.
Reflect on how you used SwiftUI components to build your first visionOS app.
Extend the Friends’ Favorite Movies project from
to relate friends to movies and to let people search for movies by title.
